mainTopic: Which items join together (מצטרפין) to reach a minimum amount: parts of offerings, kinds of תרומה, and נבילות and שקצים
overview: The משנה lists five parts of an עולה (and six of a תודה, counting its bread) that join together to reach a minimum amount. The גמרא first fixes the wording: it should read 'בעולה', in the burnt offering, not 'בעולם', in the world. It then quotes a ברייתא saying the meat and אימורים of an עולה join for a כזית. It asks why שלמים would be left out for פיגול, נותר and טמא, since a משנה says all פיגולים and all נותרים join. The answer rereads the ברייתא: an עולה's meat and אימורים join to make the כזית needed to throw the blood, and liability follows from that. This follows רבי יהושע, and רב פפא explains that the מנחה he mentions is the מנחת נסכים. A new משנה teaches that all kinds of תרומה, along with חלה and ביכורים, join together because the Torah calls them all תרומה. A third משנה says all נבילות join and all שקצים join, and רב's comment on it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The parts of an offering that combine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five parts of an עולה and six parts of a תודה that join together into one measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things in a burnt offering join together: the meat, the fat, the flour, the wine and the oil. In a thanks offering there are six: the meat, the fat, the flour, the wine, the oil and the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a list of parts of an offering that can be added together to reach a minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה comes with a flour offering (flour and oil) and a wine pouring, so all five parts count together. A תודה has those same five parts plus its special loaves of bread, which makes six.

keyTerms.meaning: they join together (to reach a minimum amount)
burnt offering, burned completely on the altar
thanks offering, which comes with loaves of bread
fine flour of the flour offering that comes with the animal
the loaves that come with a תודה

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Five items in the burnt offering
join together with one another:
phrases.notes: They join to reach the minimum amount, a פרוטה for מעילה or a כזית for eating prohibitions.

phrases.english: the flesh, the fat, the fine flour,
the wine, and the oil.
And six in the thanks offering:
the flesh, the fat, the fine flour,
the wine, the oil, and the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים בָּעוֹלָה מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five parts of an עולה, and six of a תודה (including the bread), join together toward the minimum amount.

steps.title: רב הונא's version: five items in the world
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא taught רבא the משנה with the word 'בעולם' (in the world) instead of 'בעולה' (in the burnt offering).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא taught רבא: 'Five things in the world join together.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a different wording of the משנה. This sets up רבא's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'בעולם' the משנה would mean there are only five things in all offerings that ever join together. The two words differ by one letter (ה or ם), so a mix-up is easy.

keyTerms.meaning: in the world
with one another

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna taught Rava:
"Five items in the world
join together with one another."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different wording of the משנה's opening line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא's text read 'בעולם', in the world.

steps.title: רבא objects: the thanks offering has six
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how the משנה can say only five things in the world join, when the same משנה lists six for a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You are saying 'in the world'? But the משנה itself teaches about the thanks offering that six things join: the meat, the fat, the flour, the wine, the oil and the thanks-offering bread!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the wording 'בעולם' by pointing to the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only five things 'in the world' join, a list of six for the תודה is impossible. The משנה would contradict itself, so the wording must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: you are saying?
but isn't it taught?
the loaves of the thanks offering

phrases.english: He said to him: You are saying "in the world"?
But isn't it taught regarding the thanks offering:
"six items that are in the thanks offering:
the flesh, the fat, the fine flour,
the wine, the oil, and the loaves of the thanks offering"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'בעולם' wording given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'five items in the world'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה lists six items for a תודה, so there cannot be only five in the world.

steps.title: Fix the wording to 'in the burnt offering'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is to read the משנה as 'בעולה', in the burnt offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Read it as 'in the burnt offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The wording is corrected, and the contradiction goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'בעולה' the five items describe the עולה only. That fits perfectly with six items for the תודה, which has bread as well.

keyTerms.meaning: in the burnt offering

steps.whatToRemember: The correct wording of the משנה is 'בעולה', in the burnt offering, not 'בעולם', in the world.

phrases.english: He said to him: Teach "in the burnt offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection by correcting the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says five items in all of the world of offerings join.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה says five items in an עולה join.

steps.title: A ברייתא already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that a ברייתא already taught that the meat and אימורים of an עולה join for a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned what the Rabbis taught: Burnt offerings and their altar portions join together to make an olive's size, both for offering them outside and for being liable for them because of פיגול, נותר and eating while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה matches a ברייתא that says meat and fat of an עולה combine. This sets up a question about the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two uses for combining. One is offering them outside the courtyard. The other is liability for eating them as פיגול, נותר or while impure.

keyTerms.meaning: the parts of an animal burned on the altar
an olive's size, the minimum amount for liability
offering them up outside the courtyard
an offering made unfit by a wrong intention about its time
leftover sacrificial meat past its time

phrases.english: We already learned this,
that the Sages taught:
Burnt offerings and sacrificial portions
join together to make an olive-bulk
for offering them up outside,
and to make one liable for them
due to piggul, notar, and impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording of the משנה to its content, the meat and fat combining.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The meat and אימורים of an עולה join to make a כזית for offering outside and for פיגול, נותר and טמא.

steps.title: Only burnt offerings, not peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely: it says עולה, which implies שלמים do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches: for a burnt offering, yes; for peace offerings, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא's choice of words. This prepares the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא names only עולות, the גמרא concludes that the meat and אימורים of שלמים do not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: yes
no
peace offerings, whose meat is eaten and only certain parts are burned

phrases.english: It teaches: with a burnt offering, yes;
with peace offerings, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, the meat and אימורים of שלמים do not combine.

steps.title: Why don't peace offerings combine for eating prohibitions?
steps.stepSummary: Not combining makes sense for offering outside. But why wouldn't שלמים combine for פיגול, נותר and טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for offering them outside: a burnt offering is burned completely, so its parts join, while peace offerings do not join. But for being liable because of פיגול, נותר and impurity, why is one not liable with peace offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts one half of the inference and challenges the other half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole עולה goes on the altar, so its meat and אימורים combine for offering outside. The meat of שלמים is not burned, so it would not combine there. The eating prohibitions are a different matter, and the גמרא asks why שלמים should be any different there.

keyTerms.meaning: granted, it makes sense
completely burned
but (here, introducing the difficulty)
why?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning the 'offering outside' part. It agrees that שלמים don't combine there. It only asks about the eating prohibitions.

phrases.english: Granted, with regard to offering them up outside,
a burnt offering, which is completely burned, they join;
peace offerings, they do not join.
But with regard to making one liable for them
due to piggul, notar, and impurity,
why is one not liable with peace offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference from step 6 as it applies to the eating prohibitions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that שלמים do not combine for פיגול, נותר and טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being burned completely explains combining for offering outside. It does not explain why eating prohibitions would treat שלמים differently.

steps.title: A משנה shows that all פיגול and נותר pieces join together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה to strengthen its question: all פיגולים join together and all נותרות join together, so why limit the joining to an עולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: all pieces that are פיגול join together with each other, and all pieces that are נותר join together with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its question from step 7 with a source. A משנה says that every kind of פיגול and נותר joins together to make the minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say that only an עולה's meat and אימורים join, which implies שלמים do not. But this משנה says 'all' פיגולים and 'all' נותרות join, with no limit to עולה. So the ברייתא's limit to עולה looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid because the כהן intended to eat or burn it at the wrong time
Sacrificial meat left over past the time it may be eaten
They join together (to reach the minimum amount)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: all the pieces of פיגול
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in this פרק. It speaks about every kind of offering, not just an עולה.

phrases.english: join together with one another,
and all the pieces of נותר
join together with one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: כׇּל הַפִּיגּוּלִים מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that gives the question of step 7 its force.
steps.raayaObject: That the meat and אימורים of all offerings, including שלמים, join for פיגול and נותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה: כל הפיגולים מצטרפין זה עם זה וכל הנותרות מצטרפות זו עם זו.

steps.title: Reread the ברייתא: the joining is for throwing the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the עולה's meat and אימורים join to make a כזית in order to allow throwing the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: an עולה and its אימורים join together to make a כזית, so that one may throw the blood for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the ברייתא. It is not mainly about liability for פיגול or נותר. It is about joining together so the blood may be thrown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood may only be thrown if at least a כזית of the offering is left. The ברייתא now teaches that for an עולה, a bit of meat and a bit of אימורים can add up to that כזית. That is why it names only עולה, and this no longer conflicts with the משנה about all פיגולים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא rereads the wording of a source
The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
An olive's volume, the basic minimum amount
Throwing the blood on the מזבח, the key act of the offering

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying שלמים never join for פיגול or נותר. In the new reading, the limit to עולה is about throwing the blood.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
A burnt offering and its sacrificial portions
join together with one another to make an olive's volume
to throw the blood for them.
phrases.notes: If most of the offering got lost, the blood can still be thrown as long as a כזית is left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 7–8 by changing the meaning of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא teaches that only an עולה's meat and אימורים join for liability, so שלמים would not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that an עולה's meat and אימורים join to make a כזית for throwing the blood.

steps.title: Since they join for the blood, one is liable
steps.stepSummary: Once the עולה's parts join to allow throwing the blood, one becomes liable for eating them (as פיגול, נותר or טמא), and so on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since they join together to allow throwing the blood, one is liable, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It links the joining for the blood to the liability the ברייתא mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valid זריקת הדם is what brings the laws of פיגול, נותר and טמא into effect. So the joining for the blood leads to the liability. That is why the ברייתא still talks about liability, even though its main point is the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: And since: shows that one thing leads to another
Liable to punishment
Et cetera: the rest of the quote is left out

phrases.english: And since they join together
to throw the blood,
one is liable, et cetera.
phrases.notes: Liable for eating it as פיגול, as נותר, or while טמא, as the ברייתא listed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 9 by connecting it to liability.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Cause and effect: valid blood-throwing leads to liability
steps.terutzMaskana: Joining for זריקת הדם is what makes the eater liable for פיגול, נותר and טמא in an עולה.
steps.whatToRemember: For an עולה, meat and אימורים join to make the כזית needed to throw the blood. Liability for eating follows from that.

steps.title: Who is the author of this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the meat and אימורים of an עולה join for throwing the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who teaches this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which sage is behind this ruling. This sets up the next step, which names him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule implies that in other offerings, meat and אימורים do not join for the blood. The גמרא wants to find a תנא who holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who teaches it? Asks for the author of a ruling

phrases.english: And who teaches it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the meaning of the ברייתא to who wrote it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that meat and אימורים join for זריקת הדם only in an עולה.

steps.title: It is רבי יהושע: half and half is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The author is רבי יהושע, who rules that blood is thrown if a כזית of meat or of חלב is left, but not for half a כזית of each.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהושע, as it was taught: רבי יהושע says, any offering in the תורה that has a כזית of meat or a כזית of חלב left over, one throws the blood. If only half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of חלב are left, one does not throw the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי יהושע as the author and quotes his ruling. A full כזית of meat or of חלב allows throwing the blood, but half of each does not add up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For offerings in general, רבי יהושע says meat and חלב do not join to make the כזית for the blood. Our ברייתא teaches that an עולה is different, and there they do join. So the ברייתא fits רבי יהושע's view, and it explains why it singled out עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings
Was left over (after the rest was lost or became unfit)
Fat that is burned on the מזבח
Half an olive's volume

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, meat and חלב normally do not join for throwing the blood. The ברייתא teaches that an עולה is the exception.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the ברייתא named only עולה. Joining for the blood is not automatic, so an עולה needed to be taught on its own.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהושע,
as it was taught: רבי יהושע says:
All the offerings in the תורה
from which there remained
an olive's volume of meat or an olive's volume of fat,
one throws the blood,

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב –
phrases.english: half an olive's volume of meat and half an olive's volume of fat,
one does not throw the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 by naming the author and quoting him.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יהושע, who holds that meat and חלב normally do not join for זריקת הדם (half and half is not enough). An עולה is the case where they do join.

steps.title: In a burnt offering, half and half join, but the meal offering does not count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי יהושע continues: in an עולה, half a כזית of meat plus half a כזית of חלב is enough to throw the blood, because it is all burned on the altar. With a מנחה, even if all of it remains, the blood is not thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with an עולה, even if only half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of fat are left, he throws the blood, because all of it is burned on the altar. And with the מנחה, even if all of it is still there, he does not throw the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא of רבי יהושע. This is the line that shows he holds the meat and אימורים of an עולה join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In other offerings, the meat is eaten by people and the חלב goes on the altar, so the two do not join. In an עולה both go on the altar, so they count as one thing and add up to a כזית. This is exactly the joining that Step 9 described.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering. The whole animal is burned on the altar.
About half an olive's size, half of the minimum amount.
Completely burned on the altar.
He throws the blood on the altar, the key act of the offering.

steps.whyThisMatters: This proves the answer to Step 11's question: the ברייתא about the עולה's parts joining follows רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: But with a burnt offering, even half an olive-bulk of meat
and half an olive-bulk of fat
he throws the blood,
because it is all entirely burned.
And with the meal offering, even if all of it remains
he does not throw the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָעוֹלָה, אֲפִילּוּ כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי יהושע quoted in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע explicitly rules that in an עולה, half a כזית of meat and half of חלב join to allow throwing the blood.

steps.title: Why is a meal offering mentioned here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a מנחה has to do with throwing blood. A מנחה is flour and has no blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מנחה, what is it doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the last line of the ברייתא. A flour offering has no blood, so why mention it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling 'do not throw the blood' only makes sense for something connected to an animal. The גמרא needs to know which מנחה the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offering, made of flour.
What is its business here? Why is it relevant?

phrases.english: A meal offering, what is its relevance?
phrases.notes: A מנחה has no blood at all, so the line about not throwing blood seems out of place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the last clause of the ברייתא in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מנחה could have any link to throwing an animal's blood?

steps.title: It means the meal offering brought with the libations
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא means the מנחת נסכים, the flour offering brought together with an animal sacrifice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is the מנחת נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the ברייתא is talking about the מנחה that comes along with an animal offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the מנחת נסכים belongs to the animal offering, one might think it can stand in for the missing meat. The ברייתא teaches that it cannot. If no meat or חלב is left, the blood is not thrown, even if the whole מנחה is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering brought together with an animal sacrifice and its wine.
Libations, the wine and flour that go with an animal offering.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The meal offering of libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא means the מנחת נסכים that comes with the animal. It does not count toward allowing the blood to be thrown.
steps.whatToRemember: In an עולה, the meat and חלב join to make a כזית for throwing the blood. The accompanying מנחת נסכים never counts toward this.

steps.title: New משנה: kinds of תרומה join together, as do all פיגולים and all נותרים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that תרומה, תרומת מעשר, תרומת מעשר of דמאי, חלה and ביכורים all join together. Together they can reach the amount needed to forbid a mixture and to require paying an extra חומש. All פיגולים join together, and all נותרים join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: תרומה, תרומת מעשר, תרומת מעשר of דמאי, חלה and ביכורים join with each other to forbid a mixture and to make a person pay the חומש. All פיגולים join with each other. All נותרים join with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists different holy foods that add up together to reach the minimum amount for a law to apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item alone may be too small to matter. Because these foods are counted as one family, small amounts of each add up. They then reach the amount needed to forbid ordinary food they fall into, or to make an eater pay the extra fifth. The same is true for different פיגול pieces and different נותר pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth of the מעשר that the לוי gives to the כהן.
Produce bought from someone who may not have tithed it.
The portion of dough given to the כהן.
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש.
The extra fifth paid by someone who eats תרומה by mistake.
They join together to make up the full amount.

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is the one the גמרא already quoted in Step 8 to ask its question. Here it simply appears in its own place as the next משנה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Teruma, and teruma of the tithe,
and teruma of the tithe of doubtfully tithed produce,
and challa, and first fruits
join together with one another
to forbid, and to make one liable for them to pay the fifth.
phrases.notes: 'To forbid' means making a mixture with ordinary food forbidden. The fifth is the extra payment for eating them by mistake.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַפִּיגּוּלִים – מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.english: All piggul join together with one another.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַנּוֹתָרִים – מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.english: And all notar join together with one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The various kinds of תרומה join to forbid and to require the חומש. All פיגולים join, and all נותרים join.

steps.title: Why do these different foods join?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that these different foods count together.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why the foods in the משנה's first list join together, even though they are different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally different kinds of food do not add up to one measure. The גמרא wants to know what makes these items one group.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What links תרומה, תרומת מעשר, דמאי, חלה and ביכורים so that they join?

steps.title: All of them are called תרומה, starting with חלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah calls all of them תרומה. It starts proving this with the פסוק about חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them are called תרומה. About חלה it is written: 'The first of your dough, חלה, you shall set aside as a תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: the Torah uses the word תרומה for each of these foods. It then begins showing this one by one, starting with חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah gives them all the same name, they count as one category, so their amounts add together. The proof for חלה is clear, because its פסוק says 'תרימו תרומה.' The proofs for the others continue after this.

keyTerms.meaning: They are called.
Your dough.
You shall set aside, or lift up as a gift.

phrases.english: All of them are called 'teruma.'
With regard to challa it is written:
'Of the first of your dough, challa'
'you shall set apart for a teruma,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 and starts the proof from the פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They join because the Torah calls every one of them תרומה. For חלה, the פסוק says 'תרימו תרומה.'

steps.title: ביכורים are also called תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a ברייתא that ביכורים are also called תרומה. The other items in the משנה clearly carry that name, so they need no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: ביכורים are also called 'תרומה'. A ברייתא teaches that the words 'וּתְרוּמַת יָדֶךָ' (the offering of your hand) mean ביכורים. The other items need no proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer from the last step. It shows that ביכורים are also called תרומה, so they can join with the others too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step the גמרא proved that חלה is called תרומה. Now it does the same for ביכורים, using a ברייתא that reads 'וּתְרוּמַת יָדֶךָ' as ביכורים. תרומה, תרומת מעשר and תרומת מעשר of דמאי already have 'תרומה' in their names, so the גמרא says no proof is needed for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding, about
They are called
The offering of your hand, which the ברייתא explains as ביכורים
The other ones
It is not necessary (no proof is needed)

steps.whatToRemember: Every item in the משנה is called 'תרומה' in the Torah. That shared name is why they all join together to reach a full measure.

phrases.english: Regarding first fruits, they are also called "terumah",
as it is taught: "And the offering of your hand"
these are first fruits.
But the others, it is not necessary.
phrases.notes: He means תרומה, תרומת מעשר and תרומת מעשר of דמאי. Their names already include the word 'תרומה'.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי בִּיכּוּרִים נָמֵי אִיקְּרוּ תְּרוּמָה, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 18. Step 18 proved that חלה is called תרומה, and this step adds ביכורים and sets aside the rest.
steps.raayaObject: That ביכורים are called תרומה, so they join with the other kinds of תרומה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining 'וּתְרוּמַת יָדֶךָ' (דברים 12:17) as ביכורים

steps.title: New משנה: carcasses join together, and repugnant creatures join together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that all kinds of נבילות join with each other, and all kinds of שקצים join with each other, to reach the needed measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: All animal carcasses (נבילות) join together with one another. All repugnant creatures (שקצים) join together with one another.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two more groups of forbidden things that combine to make a full measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the topic was different kinds of תרומה joining together. Now the משנה adds two more groups: meat from different animals that died without proper שחיטה, and different kinds of שקצים. Within each group, small amounts can be added together to reach the size needed for the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Animal carcasses, animals that died without proper שחיטה
Repugnant creatures that are forbidden to eat
They join together (to reach the needed measure)

phrases.english: MISHNA

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנְּבֵילוֹת – מִצְטָרְפִין זוֹ עִם זוֹ.
phrases.english: All animal carcasses join together with one another.
phrases.notes: 'Join together' means small pieces from different carcasses add up to the needed size, which is a כזית.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַשְּׁקָצִים – מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.english: And all repugnant creatures join together with one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַנְּבֵילוֹת מִצְטָרְפִין זוֹ עִם זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with the same theme as step 16: forbidden items that join together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All נבילות join together with each other, and all שקצים join together with each other, to make up the needed measure.

steps.title: The גמרא opens with a statement of רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins discussing the new משנה by introducing a statement of רב. The statement itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by introducing a teaching from רב about the משנה. What רב says continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the משנה, the גמרא turns to רב to explain it, probably the part about נבילות joining together. Only the opening words appear on this amud. רב's statement itself continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav says:
phrases.notes: What רב says continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the משנה in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. רב's teaching continues on the next amud.
